release: review-only; no print or powered-operation admission
readme:
A16 inlet duct for a Delta BFB1012M radial blower laid FLAT on the plug end. Generated from product.printed_chassis.gpu_duct.
Admitted by product.printed_chassis.card_cooling_route on the operator's declared conservative bounds of 2026-10-26: 70 mm behind the plug end ('i would put 70mm for now - its like 73mm but i want to be conservative') and ample space on the sides ('yes, you can assume more than enough space on the sides, 70mm is fine'). Neither is a caliper reading, and the print is admitted on that ruling anyway: one PLA plate is the cheapest instrument available, and this part is it. Report what you find -- whether the housing clears the rear fan, and whether it clears the next card -- so the bound becomes a reading.
What goes back is the housing's thickness plus the SEAT it rests on: 33.0 mm of thickness with its cited +/-0.5 mm tolerance, on a printed seat 7.5 mm deep -- 41.0 mm behind the end face (plane_on_end_duct_run_back). The seat is not padding: the blower's bottom face used to sit 2 mm behind the face, inside the 7 mm the plugged 8-pin head reaches, and the fan cannot be moved, so the printed part is what moved. It is sized at the head's worst-case reach plus this print's own edge allowance on BOTH of the faces in the gap -- never flush, because at exactly the reach it would be flush and flush on a +/-0.5 mm print is zero clearance. What it is checked against is the TIGHTEST reading of that span, not the most generous: the 2026-10-26 allowance was 70 mm, but on 2026-10-29 the operator read the card's back end to the 120 mm fan at 60 mm ('The gap from the card's back end to the 120 mm chassis fan is 60 mm, not the 70 mm your headroom used'), carried at 59 mm with the width on a by-eye figure, so 18 mm is what is actually to spare. What it spends is width: the 97.2 mm edge runs across the slot and overhangs this card's lane by 28.28 mm on each side. One card only -- two adjacent housings would face each other's intakes across 5.04 mm.
The collector is an OPEN SHOULDER, not a spigot, because the outlet's position on Delta's housing is unread: the whole band of the housing's periphery that faces the card is left open, so any outlet position in it feeds the window.
KNOWN OPEN POINT, AND IT IS THE SHARP ONE: the housing cannot be placed clear of the 8-pin power connector's keep-out in either orientation. The A16 end face is 97.84 mm and the connector claims a 26 mm band at its top end (2.56 mm from the edge to the connector's near pin), leaving 71.84 mm clear; the BFB1012M housing is 94.4 mm at its SHORTER edge and 97.2 mm at its longer one. The housing therefore lies over the connector's band wherever it goes on this face -- not a placement mistake, a size fact. Read the presentation fields power_keepout_crossing_um, face_clear_of_power_keepout_um and housing_shorter_edge_um. The kernel's POWER-KEEPOUT check decides whether this part is allowed through; an operator who wants it anyway is overruling a keep-out and should say so out loud.
PLUGGED IN, NOT BARE: fit and check this part WITH THE 8-PIN POWERED IN -- 'The plugged 8-pin head protrudes 6 mm, and the cable bends almost as soon as it leaves the head' (2026-10-29), carried at 7 mm worst case. Three things follow, and all three are printed, not assumed. (1) The relief window over the connector band opens the shoulder floor AND the seat across the connector's own band, so the head and the cable's turn have no printed wall in front of them; the head sits 7 mm in a 25.5 mm window. (2) The SEAT lifts the blower's bottom face to 7.5 mm behind the end face, clearing the head by 0.5 mm derived -- the head no longer crushes the fan. (3) The connector latch ('the plug latch is 3 mm', carried at 4 mm) is accommodated, not cut: nobody is asked to cut the plug.
WHAT THE FIT PRINT IS FOR -- report these, they are not gated by anything except one PLA plate: (a) dress the cable plugged in and confirm it really stays in the plane of the card end; a run that dips to 4 mm or shallower on its way INBOARD of the relief's edge meets the seat's end face instead (product.printed_chassis.card_cooling_route cable_bend_path names that surface and its depth); (b) the head clears the fan -- report the gap you see under the seat, since 0.5 mm is what is derived and a print is not a caliper; (c) the duct seats on the card end with no rocking and the flange lies flat; (d) the blower seats on the shoulder with its bottom face over the open relief window -- that window is 78 mm wide and the face spans it unsupported by design, so say whether the fan sits flat or sags into it; (e) whether the housing clears the rear chassis fan and the next card, so the operator's declared bounds become readings.
DUCT.stl prints shoulder-down and needs support under the collector's roof. Drive both M3 x 4 screws into the end cap through the flange before the blower goes down. PLA for an unpowered fit check; PETG or ASA for service.

Decided by the kernel's POWER-KEEPOUT check, and by the operator if they overrule it -- not by this model.

parts.name: Inlet duct: BFB1012M flat on the plug end, open shoulder and turned collector into the fin window
parts.notes: Print shoulder-down; the shoulder floor is solid, the housing pocket is open upward and open toward the card along the whole outlet band, and the collector's roof needs support. Drive both M3 x 4 screws into the end cap's inserts through the flange BEFORE the blower goes down, then drop the housing into the pocket with its intake facing the rear chassis fan. The 8-pin connector keep-out is CROSSED by the shoulder's top-end corner (26.28 mm) and the operator admitted it; the floor over the connector's band is relieved away so the plugged header and its 3 mm latch sit in a cleared window -- fit-test it PLUGGED, and if anything protrudes behind the end more than 36.5 mm (plane_on_end_max_admissible_protrusion) the home refuses and the latch must come off or the blower must move forward. PLA for an unpowered fit prototype only; PETG or ASA for service.

parts.notes: Bounding envelope only: the housing lies flat, 94.4 mm along the end face and 97.2 mm across the slot, 33 mm thick along the card's length with Delta's tolerance. Housing cited to Delta's BFB sheet (extdeps.fans.delta delta_bfb1012m_envelope_standing); the outlet's position along the peripheral band is uncited (delta_bfb1012m_outlet_standing), which is why the collector is an open shoulder and not a spigot.
